topic: Constant Contact holiday shopper retention gap

caption:
Holiday shopper checklist: 4 ways Black-owned businesses can keep the new customers this small business season brings in.

Constant Contact released its Small Business Now Holiday Report on November 3, 2026. It surveyed more than 1,800 small business owners and 2,600 shoppers in the US, Canada, the UK, Australia and New Zealand. Three in four shoppers say they're likely to try a small business they've never bought from. More than 70% of owners have no plan to invite those new shoppers onto an email list or loyalty program.

Here's what to have ready before the rush:
1. A QR code on every bag, receipt and package that opens your signup page.
2. A website signup that takes ten seconds on a phone.
3. Packaging and receipts with your logo and colors, so they remember who you are.
4. A thank you email ready to go, with a reason to come back in January.

Nearly half of shoppers (48.5%) choose small businesses for original gifts. They came for what makes you different. Make it easy to find you again.

caption_drafts.explainer:
The Constant Contact holiday report has a warning for small businesses and Black-owned businesses: you'll win new customers this season and lose most of them by January.

The report came out November 3, 2026. Three in four shoppers plan to try a small business they've never bought from. More than 70% of owners have no plan to invite them onto an email list or loyalty program, and only 39% plan to send follow up emails in the new year.

Shoppers pick small businesses for original gifts (48.5%) and a better shopping experience (43.9%). That first visit is your brand's one shot to be remembered.

caption_drafts.provocation:
Small business owners, what happens to the stranger who buys from you on Small Business Saturday? Constant Contact's new holiday report says most Black-owned businesses and small shops will never hear from them again.

The November 3 report found three in four shoppers want to try a new small business this season. More than 70% of owners have no plan to get those shoppers onto an email list or loyalty program.

Picture two shops with the same great product. One hands over a bag with a logo and a QR code to sign up. The other hands over a plain bag. In January, only one of them can say hello.
